decisions.statement: A caller writes a change's arguments on standard input rather than as flags.
A scalar argument is a key and the rest of the line after that key's colon.
A body argument is a key and the fence that body ends at.
A fence is the word the caller picks rather than a word this module fixes.
A body holds each line up to the fence.
A line in a body keeps its newline.
A body whose opening line closes with `no-newline` drops the newline off its last line.
A passage ending mid-line is said that way and no other way.
Nothing in a body is escaped.
Nothing in a body is counted.
A body no fence closes refuses the whole reading.
A key written twice refuses the whole reading.
A line of neither form refuses the whole reading.
Nothing here reads a file or reaches an index.
Which arguments a change takes is answered by that change rather than here.
A body with the fence the caller picked ends at that line early.

definition: the arguments a change is handed, read from what a caller wrote on standard input
